sn37.1:1.1: _Mātugāma_ literally means “motherkind” (cf. the archaic “motherkin”). It is a word for women in Pali, but it appears unique to Buddhist texts, and hence may be a quasi-technical term (cf. _puggala_, [sn22.22:2.2]()). Grammatically it is always singular, but it is used in both singular and plural senses. We can see this here: in this sentence, it must be “womankind” in general since it is paired with “men” in plural, whereas below it is paired with “man” so must be “woman”. The commentary says it is any human woman, even one born that very day. Probably the term “mother” is meant in an affectionate and respectful sense (cf. [sn35.127:1.6]()), so to distinguish from _itthī_ as “woman” I use “lady” for _mātugāma_. “Lady” is also used in some other cases, but context should help disambiguate.  Throughout the Pātimokkha it is used in apposition with _bhikkhu_, whereas _itthī_ (“woman”_) is used with _purisa_ (“man”). But there is no corresponding male form, so _bhikkhunī_ just takes _purisa_. However, this does not obtain here, where _mātugāma_ is used with _purisa_.
